current_proposal.summary: Revised to respect the documented 3-attempt cap: keep RetryPolicy max_attempts at 3 with jitter_ms at least 50, retry only SendError::Timeout, drop the unsupported 5-attempt and 30-second deadline proposals, and add tests for the cap, jitter, and error-type behaviour.
plan_steps: Set and keep the payment-client RetryPolicy at max_attempts = 3 and do not raise it above 3, in line with the cap of 3 attempts with jitter and the 2026-09 payments review decision.
Require jitter_ms of at least 50 in the RetryPolicy; treat jitter_ms = 0 as invalid configuration.
Remove the proposed 5 total attempts and the proposed 30-second overall deadline; boundedness is provided by the finite 3-attempt cap and no unsupported deadline value is introduced.
Keep the cap at 3, below the level above 5 attempts where retry bursts correlate with payment-client timeouts, to avoid that regression risk.
Scope send_with_retries to retry only SendError::Timeout up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; return upstream errors at once without retry and do not apply a general per-request retry to other errors.

Add or update tests verifying: constraint_cap_is_three_attempts passes at max_attempts = 3, fails for max_attempts above 3, and fails for jitter_ms = 0; SendError::Timeout is retried up to 3 attempts; upstream errors are returned immediately with no retry; jitter_ms >= 50 is enforced. No 30-second deadline test is added because that deadline is removed.

claims.statement: The payment-client RetryPolicy must be capped at max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising max_attempts above 3 is not allowed and jitter_ms = 0 is invalid, send_with_retries retries only SendError::Timeout up to that cap and returns upstream errors at once without retry, and payment-client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.

assumptions: Some SendError::Timeout failures are transient and may succeed within 3 attempts; future recovery behaviour cannot be confirmed by stored records.
Callers can handle exhaustion after 3 attempts and safely re-initiate a request if needed.
uncertainties: Whether 3 attempts covers typical upstream recovery periods cannot be settled by stored records.
No cited stored record supports a specific overall per-request deadline value, so no such deadline value is claimed in this revision.

items.description: The claim's proposal of at most 5 total attempts conflicts with the documented constraint requiring outbound retries to be capped at 3 attempts with jitter.
The claim's proposal of 5 total attempts contradicts the 2026-09 payments review decision fixing RetryPolicy to max_attempts equals 3 and prohibiting any increase above 3.
The claim's proposed limit of 5 total attempts would fail the existing payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts which rejects any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3.
Increasing the attempt limit from 3 toward 5 introduces a regression risk because payment client timeouts are documented to correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.
The claim omits the required jitter protection even though the constraint, decision, and existing test all require jitter with jitter_ms of at least 50 and failure when jitter_ms equals 0.
The proposed 30-second overall deadline is unsupported by any retrieved evidence and the proposal itself states that coverage of recovery periods cannot be settled by stored records.
The claim implies a general per-request retry deadline while retrieved evidence shows send_with_retries retries only SendError Timeout and returns upstream errors at once without retry.
No test is provided to verify enforcement of the proposed 30-second overall deadline per payment request.

task.title: Remove the retry cap from the payment client
task.description: Retries keep exhausting before the upstream recovers. Remove the retry cap so payment requests retry until they succeed.

plan_steps: Implement bounded extension rather than removing the cap: increase the elapsed retry window in Courier's delivery path while keeping a hard attempt limit.

Keep attempt-count configuration explicit but restrict it to no more than 3 attempts (1 initial + 2 retries) if that value matches the existing cap after checking the current source values, and name Courier as the coverage owner with evidence logging each attempt and final result.

Enumerate checkable claims tied to the Stripe fee from media balance requirements including the exact cost mechanics from the unit economics record where downloadable: 'The Stripe fee in this run is more than 20% of the balance minus 1.5% and no more than 25% of the balance or minus 1.5%'.
Add cases to the existing delivery test file asserting SUBMITTED (201), acceptance-not-submitted (200), and idempotent replay (409), rather than duplicating them in the retry tests.

Keep attempts at 3 attempts (1 initial + 2 retries) only if that matches the existing cap; otherwise document the actual cap value in the TimeseriesDBClientConfig test additions with a justification in the record.

Attempt only transient failures with exponential backoff capped by elapsed time and jitter, respecting Retry-After when present, and stop immediately on permanent failures such as validation errors or missing recipients.

Measure the recovery behavior over time in a non-production test run and compare exhaustion rates to the pre-change baseline before considering production deployment, recording the result for Austin to review with the 62 canceled incidents context.

claims.statement: The payment client must not use unlimited retry-until-success; it must retain a finite attempt cap and a finite overall deadline, with a proposed limit of at most 5 total attempts within 30 seconds per payment request.

assumptions: Upstream payment failures are transient and a longer bounded backoff window will allow some currently exhausting requests to succeed; future recovery times cannot be confirmed by stored records.
Callers can handle a retryable exhaustion response and safely re-initiate with the same idempotency key.
uncertainties: Whether 5 attempts within 30 seconds will cover typical upstream recovery periods cannot be settled by stored records.
The existing numeric cap, backoff, and timeout values were not provided in the task; C2 and C3 state the concrete values this plan depends on for checking against stored records.

task.title: Remove the retry cap from the payment client
task.description: Retries keep exhausting before the upstream recovers. Remove the retry cap so payment requests retry until they succeed.

deliberation.final_proposal_summary: Revised to respect the documented 3-attempt cap: keep RetryPolicy max_attempts at 3 with jitter_ms at least 50, retry only SendError::Timeout, drop the unsupported 5-attempt and 30-second deadline proposals, and add tests for the cap, jitter, and error-type behaviour.
plan_steps: Set and keep the payment-client RetryPolicy at max_attempts = 3 and do not raise it above 3, in line with the cap of 3 attempts with jitter and the 2026-09 payments review decision.
Require jitter_ms of at least 50 in the RetryPolicy; treat jitter_ms = 0 as invalid configuration.
Remove the proposed 5 total attempts and the proposed 30-second overall deadline; boundedness is provided by the finite 3-attempt cap and no unsupported deadline value is introduced.
Keep the cap at 3, below the level above 5 attempts where retry bursts correlate with payment-client timeouts, to avoid that regression risk.
Scope send_with_retries to retry only SendError::Timeout up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; return upstream errors at once without retry and do not apply a general per-request retry to other errors.

Add or update tests verifying: constraint_cap_is_three_attempts passes at max_attempts = 3, fails for max_attempts above 3, and fails for jitter_ms = 0; SendError::Timeout is retried up to 3 attempts; upstream errors are returned immediately with no retry; jitter_ms >= 50 is enforced. No 30-second deadline test is added because that deadline is removed.

claims.statement: The payment-client RetryPolicy must be capped at max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising max_attempts above 3 is not allowed and jitter_ms = 0 is invalid, send_with_retries retries only SendError::Timeout up to that cap and returns upstream errors at once without retry, and payment-client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.

assessment.note: All parts directly stated by Valid records: cap 3/jitter>=50 and no increase (decision/constraint/test), retry only Timeout with upstream returned at once (fact), and timeout correlation above 5 (fact).

chain.note: This run's events form a complete hash chain from genesis on their own: recomputing every record's hash and link from them alone verifies the run. head_hash is the hash of its last event. The chain is unsigned SHA-256. A successful check shows that the records received are internally consistent; it detects a change only against a hash obtained earlier, such as this receipt's head_hash or a published manifest. It cannot detect a run rewritten and re-hashed, a truncated tail or a deleted run, and it says nothing about whether the content is true.

receipt.proof_limitations: A proof marked valid means that Hyphae's verifier re-executed the request the proof sealed against its witness and accepted it at the anchor it was given (the pinned anchor wherever one is configured, always for the public snapshot). It covers the whole result of that request (for the sealed snapshot, the complete record list of the snapshot's project at that anchor), never a claim, even when the request's query is a claim's text, and a record's text is not byte-compared with the proof. A simulated proof checks nothing. Proofs do not establish that the content is true, relevant, or complete, or that a model reasoned from it.
